Although [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] have frequently been in the same division in [[football in England|English football]] since 1919, the rivalry between the two clubs only became a fierce one in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when the teams regularly competed against each other for the [[Premier League]] title and the [[FA Cup]]. There was also an enmity between the managers, Arsenal's [[Arsène Wenger]] (1996–2018) and United's Sir [[Alex Ferguson]] (1986–2013), as well as club [[Captain (association football)|captains]] [[Patrick Vieira]] and [[Roy Keane]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The bitter rivalry between Arsenal and Manchester United |last1=Leach |first1=Jimmy |last2=Rice |first2=Simon |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=29 April 2009|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/the-bitter-rivalry-between-arsenal-and-manchester-united-1676014.html |access-date=9 August 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3946025.stm |title=Ferguson and Wenger 'are friends' |work=BBC Sport|date=23 October 2004 |access-date=9 August 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Myles |last=Palmer |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/oct/24/newsstory.sport4 |title=Fergie owes knighthood to Wenger the 'flat-track bully' |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=24 October 2004 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Their contests often involved on-field trouble – seven red cards were shown in matches from February 1997 to February 2005.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://lebuzz.eurosport.co.uk/quizzes/quiz-manchester-united-v-arsenal-14-red-cards-in-the-wenger-era-how-many-can-you-recall-21979/|title=Quiz: Manchester United v Arsenal: 14 red cards in the Wenger era – how many can you recall?|date=17 November 2016|access-date=30 August 2017|work=Eurosport|archive-date=31 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831045946/http://lebuzz.eurosport.co.uk/quizzes/quiz-manchester-united-v-arsenal-14-red-cards-in-the-wenger-era-how-many-can-you-recall-21979/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The league fixture in September 2003, known as the "[[Battle of Old Trafford]]", was marred by a mêlée instigated by Arsenal players, who felt striker [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] had cheated to get Vieira sent off. A season later, Manchester United [[Battle of the Buffet|ended Arsenal's unbeaten run]] in controversial circumstances, which led to more disorder, this time in the tunnel. 

By 2008, former Arsenal player [[Lee Dixon]] noted that the rivalry had diminished.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gareth |last=A Davies |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2291799/Arsenal-heroes-relish-rivalry-with-Man-Utd.html |title=Arsenal heroes relish rivalry with Man Utd |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=15 February 2008 |access-date=15 August 2009}}</ref> Ferguson also stated that the two teams' meetings had cooled from their previous "heated" exchanges.<ref name="manutd"/> Other factors for the diminishing importance of the rivalry in the 2010s were the ascendancy of other clubs, including local rivals of both ([[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]).<ref>{{cite web |last=Moody |first=Jon |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-manchester-united-rivalry-over-10361086 |title=9 reasons the Arsenal vs Manchester United rivalry has died a death in recent years |work=[[Daily Mirror]] |date=30 November 2017 |access-date=26 December 2017}}</ref>

Arsenal and Manchester United first played a competitive match in October 1894; as of 25 January 2026, the clubs have faced each other 246 times, with United winning 100 games to Arsenal's 91, and 55 matches drawn. [[Wayne Rooney]] scored the most goals in the fixture (12), while [[Ryan Giggs]] made the highest number of appearances (50). Several players have featured for both clubs at different stages of their career, including [[Brian Kidd]], [[Andy Cole]], [[David Platt (footballer)|David Platt]], [[Robin van Persie]], [[Danny Welbeck]], [[Alexis Sánchez]] and [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]].<ref name="@">{{cite news |title=12 players who featured for both Arsenal and Manchester United – and where they performed best |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/11091380/12-players-who-featured-for-both-Arsenal-and-Manchester-United-and-where-they-performed-best.html |access-date=7 November 2017 |website=The Telegraph}}</ref>

==History==
===Origins===
A particularly memorable match between the two sides came on 1 February 1958, when they met in a league fixture at [[Arsenal Stadium|Highbury]].<ref name="babes">{{cite news |first=Robert |last=Philip |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2290978/Busby-Babes-last-and-finest-league-game.html |title=Busby Babes' last – and finest – league game |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=5 February 2008 |access-date=15 August 2009}}</ref> It was the last league game that United played before the [[Munich air disaster]] five days later, which claimed the lives of eight of their players and saw two other players injured to such an extent that they never played again.<ref name="babes" /> United won the game 5–4, with goals from [[Tommy Taylor]] (twice), [[Duncan Edwards]], [[Bobby Charlton]] and [[Dennis Viollet]].<ref name="babes" /> Five of the United players who would lose their lives as a result of the crash took to the field in the game – captain and full-back [[Roger Byrne]], right-half [[Eddie Colman]], centre-half [[Mark Jones (footballer, born 1933)|Mark Jones]], left-half Edwards and centre-forward Taylor.<ref name="babes" />

Another high-profile clash came more than 20 years later, in the [[1979 FA Cup final|final]] of the [[FA Cup]] on 12 May 1979.<ref name="seven">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/history/the-seventies/-the-five-minute-final-stuns-manchester-utd |title='The Five Minute Final' stuns Manchester Utd |publisher=Arsenal FC |date=10 May 2017 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> A capacity crowd saw Arsenal take a 2–0 lead in the first half thanks to goals from [[Brian Talbot]] and [[Frank Stapleton]], and with just five minutes left on the clock their lead was still intact.<ref name="seven"/> Then, in the 86th minute, [[Gordon McQueen]] pulled a goal back for United, and two minutes later they equalised with a goal from [[Sammy McIlroy]].<ref name="seven"/> However, barely a minute after United equalised, Arsenal's [[Alan Sunderland]] scored an 89th-minute goal to win the cup 3–2 for Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/30804542 |title=FA Cup Archive: Arsenal survive Cup scare |work=BBC Sport |date=27 January 2015 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref>

Although Arsenal and Manchester United had previously contested many significant matches, Sir [[Alex Ferguson]] believed the rivalry started in January 1987 when [[David Rocastle]] was [[ejection (sports)|sent off]] for retaliating against a foul on [[Norman Whiteside]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Jonathan |last=Northcroft |title=Rivalry renewed |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/sir-alex-ferguson-and-arsene-wenger-rivalry-renewed-bsv69sld6g7 |newspaper=The Sunday Times |date=19 April 2009 |access-date=15 August 2009}} {{subscription required}}</ref> In October 1990, a [[Manchester United F.C.–Arsenal F.C. brawl (1990)|brawl]] between both sides at Old Trafford resulted in both clubs being docked points in the [[1990–91 Football League First Division|1990–91 First Division]].<ref name="manutd">{{cite news |title=Old foes, new rivalry |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Apr/Old-foes-new-rivalry.aspx |publisher=Manchester United |date=29 April 2009 |access-date=29 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Fleming |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/battle-grounds-the-history-of-arsenal-and-uniteds-emnity-2239630.html |title=Battle Grounds: The history of Arsenal and United's emnity &#91;sic&#93; |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=12 March 2011 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> The scuffle started when Arsenal's [[Anders Limpar]], who scored the only goal of the game, contested for the ball with Manchester United defender [[Denis Irwin]].<ref name="guad">{{cite news |first=Stephen |last=Bierley |title=FA to act over 21-man brawl |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=22 October 1990 |page=16 }}</ref> Limpar's teammate [[Nigel Winterburn]] tackled Irwin, which prompted [[Brian McClair]] and Irwin to retaliate.<ref name="guad"/> Winterburn was pushed onto the advertising hoardings and all the players bar goalkeeper [[David Seaman]] partook in a 20-second mêlée.<ref name="les2003">{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Hart |title=1990 – the brawl to end them all |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/1990--the-brawl-to-end-them-all-6952813.html |newspaper=Evening Standard|location=London|date=25 September 2003 |access-date=9 November 2017}}</ref> As well as a points deduction, both clubs fined several of their players, and in Arsenal's case, their manager too.<ref>{{cite news |first=Stuart |last=Jones |title=Arsenal and United count the cost |newspaper=The Times |location=London |date=13 November 1990 |page=40 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Louise |last=Taylor |title=Graham is fined by Arsenal |newspaper=The Times |location=London |date=24 October 1990 |page=42 }}</ref> Arsenal and United next faced each other at Highbury just over a month later in the [[1990–91 Football League Cup|Football League Cup]] fourth round.<ref name="six">{{cite news |first=Rob |last=Smyth |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2008/apr/11/thejoyofsixmanchesterutd |title=The Joy of Six: Manchester Utd v Arsenal showdowns |website=The Guardian|date=11 April 2008 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> 19-year-old winger [[Lee Sharpe]] scored a hat-trick as United won the tie 6–2.<ref name="six"/>

===1996–2003===
{{quote box
|width = 27%
|border = 1px
|align = right
|halign = left
|quote = He has no experience of English football. He has come from ''Japan'' and now he is telling us how to organise our football. Unless you have been in the situation and had the experience, then he should keep his mouth shut – firmly shut.
|source =— Alex Ferguson, speaking about Arsène Wenger in 1997.<ref>{{cite news |last=Caulkin |first=George |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/ferguson-s-defence-lacks-credence-1.59798 |title=Ferguson's defence lacks credence |date=7 April 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]}}</ref>}}

The rivalry intensified following the arrival of [[Arsène Wenger]] in October 1996.<ref>{{cite news |first=Alex |last=Trickett |title=Ferguson's defining moments |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/4032171.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=23 November 2004 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> The first meeting between Ferguson's United and Wenger's Arsenal took place at United's [[Old Trafford]] stadium on 16 November 1996. Arsenal went into the game unbeaten in 10 matches, but an [[own goal]] by Arsenal [[defender (association football)|defender]] [[Nigel Winterburn]] gave United a 1–0 victory. An incident in the first half involving United [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Peter Schmeichel]] and Arsenal [[Forward (association football)|striker]] [[Ian Wright]] evoked memories of the 1990 brawl.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ridley |first=Ian |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-deflected-glory-for-united-1352876.html |title=Deflected glory for United |date=17 November 1996 |access-date=22 August 2020 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> The return fixture at Highbury, a 2–1 win for United, was again marred by an incident between Wright and Schmeichel; the striker challenged for the ball with both feet and caught the goalkeeper with his studs.<ref name="mu">{{cite news |title=Wright in trouble as United pull away |first=David |last=Lacey |page=26 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=20 February 1997}}</ref> A confrontation ensued and police stepped in to keep the players apart after the final whistle.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/schmeichel-faces-racist-abuse-charge-1279851.html|title=Schmeichel faces racist abuse charge|date=21 February 1997|access-date=8 November 2013|work=The Independent}}</ref> It soon transpired the two incidents were linked, as Wright had accused Schmeichel of racially abusing him and the allegations were being criminally investigated.
<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/schmeichel-in-deep-trouble-1.45244 |title=Schmeichel in deep trouble |date=21 February 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=King |first=Rob |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/schmeichel-faces-racist-abuse-charge-1279851.html |title=Schmeichel faces racist abuse charge |date=21 February 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> Speaking to [[Sky Sports]], Ferguson firmly denied the allegations aimed at Schmeichel, and said the claims were a "slur" against the club.<ref name="SchmeichelInnocent">{{cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/schmeichel-is-innocent-ferguson-1.45667 |title=Schmeichel is innocent – Ferguson |date=21 February 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]}}</ref> Wenger claimed Ferguson was speaking too much and should let the justices do their job,<ref name="SchmeichelInnocent"/> but was defensive of the tackle which Wright had made, saying there had been 30 worse tackles in the season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Duxbury |first=Nick |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/ferguson-stands-up-for-schmeichel-1280049.html |title=Ferguson stands up for Schmeichel |date=22 February 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> Wright's behaviour was scrutinised at a hearing, where he complained he was subject to racial abuse by Schmeichel, at which point the FA intervened and met with representatives of both clubs.<ref name="mu"/> In March, it was announced that Schmeichel would not face any charges for the allegations, and the pair were asked to make a public reconciliation, with Wright agreeable to the idea,<ref>{{cite news |last=Whitfield |first=Pete |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/schmeichel-escapes-race-charge-football-1272474.html |title=Schmeichel escapes race charge |date=12 March 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> but it wasn't until April that they agreed to settle their differences.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-peace-breaks-out-in-wright-feud-1266505.html |title=Peace breaks out in Wright 'feud' |date=11 April 1997 |access-date=22 August 2020 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> The managers' animosity towards each other started to become apparent.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wright to end feud |first=Harry |last=Harris |pages=40, 44 |newspaper=The Mirror |location=London |date=27 February 1997}}</ref> 

[[File:Gary Neville 2012.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Gary Neville]] described Arsenal's 1998 side as "experienced and strong, both mentally and physically."{{sfn|Neville|2011|p=98}}]]

Wenger had advised against the Premier League extending the season to ease Manchester United's fixture congestion, to which Ferguson publicly retorted: "Maybe he should concentrate on Ian Wright's tackles rather than Manchester United. He's at a big club, well Arsenal used to be a big club, and maybe next year he could be in the same situation. I wonder what [h]is story will be then."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-wenger-incurs-the-wrath-of-ferguson-1265688.html |title=Wenger incurs the wrath of Ferguson |date=6 April 1997 |access-date=22 August 2017 |work=[[The Independent]] |location=London }}</ref>

United had won four of the first five editions of the newly branded league, and were on course to continue their domination after opening up a sizeable lead in February 1998.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-now-united-can-focus-on-europe-1147805.html |title=Now United can focus on Europe |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |first=Glenn |last=Moore |date=2 March 1998 |access-date=23 August 2017}}</ref> Injuries and poor results however destabilised the team, and by the time Arsenal visited Old Trafford in March, a title race was looking probable.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wenger and the last roll of the dice |first=Paul |last=Hayward |page=40 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=14 March 1998}}</ref> Wenger was bullish of his team's chances: "I told you last week that the race was not over when the bookmakers stopped betting. Surprise, surprise, they have started taking money again."<ref>{{cite news |title=Bookmakers resume taking bets |page=16 |newspaper=New Straits Times |location=Kuala Lumpur |date=13 March 1998}}</ref> A goal from [[Marc Overmars]] set Arsenal on the way to victory, which put them six points behind with three games in hand.<ref>{{cite news |title=Overmars keeps title race alive |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/65594.stm |work=BBC News|date=14 March 1998 |access-date=22 August 2017}}</ref> They eventually won the [[1997–98 FA Premier League|league]], and secured the [[Double (association football)|double]] by beating [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the [[1998 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Overmars provides the driving force |first=Oliver |last=Holt |page=31 |newspaper=The Times |date=18 May 1998}}</ref>
{{Quote box |width=265px |bgcolor=#FFEFD5 |salign=left |align=left |quote="It was a trauma for us. I can still hear the shouts of their team having won, they couldn’t believe it because they were down to 10 men. And I think that put them on a wave of euphoria and then they won the title – just."|source=—[[Arsène Wenger]] reflecting on the FA Cup semi-final replay<ref>{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Doyle |title=Arsène Wenger still haunted by that Ryan Giggs FA Cup goal in 1999 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/mar/07/arsenal-arsene-wenger-haunted-ryan-giggs-fa-cup-goal |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=7 March 2015 |access-date=22 August 2017}}</ref>}}

Arsenal began the 1998–99 season with a 3–0 win over United in the [[1998 FA Charity Shield|Charity Shield]]; Ferguson was unconcerned by the result, but losing to the champions a month later by the same scoreline was, in his words, "a lot less tolerable."{{sfn|Ferguson|2011|p=361}} Both clubs again vied for domestic honours; United this time pipped Arsenal by a point to regain the title.<ref name="treb">{{cite news |title='The celebrations begun by that goal will never stop |first=Oliver |last=Holt |pages=36–37 |newspaper=The Times |date=7 August 1999}}</ref> They also met in the FA Cup semi-final, which [[Arsenal F.C. 1–2 Manchester United F.C. (1999)|was replayed]] after the original game ended goalless.<ref name="semi">{{cite news |title=Giggs wonder goal is final thrill |first=Oliver |last=Holt |page=52 |newspaper=The Times |date=15 April 1999}}</ref> [[David Beckham]] and [[Dennis Bergkamp]] scored for their respective clubs either side of half time, [[Roy Keane]] was dismissed, and the holders late on were awarded a penalty.<ref name="semi"/> Schmeichel saved Bergkamp's attempt and the tie went into extra time. [[Ryan Giggs]] memorably scored the winner, picking up possession on the halfway line and dribbling past the entire Arsenal back line before shooting past [[David Seaman]].<ref name="semi"/> "A match that had everything finished with a pitch invasion, sporadic fighting and David Beckham carried shoulder-high from the field" wrote [[Matt Dickinson (journalist)|Matt Dickinson]] in ''[[The Times]]''.<ref>{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Dickinson |title=Ferguson revels in poetic justice of United's win |newspaper=The Times |page=48 |date=15 April 1999}}</ref> United went on to complete the [[Treble (association football)|Treble]], becoming the first English club to do so.<ref name="treb"/>

The rivalry continued into the new millennium, though Manchester United's domestic grip tightened. They finished 18 points clear of Arsenal in [[1999–2000 FA Premier League|1999–2000]] and completed a hat-trick of titles [[2000–01 FA Premier League|the following season]].<ref name="goldtit">{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Golden years: The tale of Manchester United's 20 titles |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21878651 |work=BBC Sport|date=22 April 2013 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Any indication United could be caught faded once Ferguson's team resoundingly beat Arsenal 6–1 in February 2001.<ref name="titl">{{cite news|url=http://www.eurosport.co.uk/all-sports/manchester-united-v-arsenal-10-famous-matches_sto4708559/story.shtml |title=Manchester United v Arsenal: 10 famous matches|date=8 November 2013|access-date=24 August 2017|publisher=Eurosport}}</ref> [[Dwight Yorke]] scored a hat-trick, on a day Wenger fielded a relatively inexperienced centre-back pairing of [[Gilles Grimandi]] and [[Igors Stepanovs (footballer, born 1976)|Igors Stepanovs]].<ref name="titl"/> At the end of the campaign, Ferguson announced his decision to retire.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/1338641.stm |title=Ferguson to quit Man Utd in 2002|date=18 May 2001|access-date=24 August 2017|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He reportedly sanctioned a bid to sign midfielder [[Patrick Vieira]], who was upset at Arsenal's transfer inactivity. The transfer never came through; Wenger blamed his rivals for "...approach[ing] to Patrick without contacting us, and that does not really respect the rules."<ref>{{cite news |title=United tried to poach unsettled Vieira, says Wenger |newspaper=The Times |first=Russell |last=Kempson |date=18 July 2001 |page=30}}</ref> United made an indifferent start to the league campaign, and by February 2002, Ferguson went back on his retirement plan on the advice of his family.<ref>{{cite news |first=Henry |last=Winter |title=Ferguson's U-turn delights United |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2430032/Fergusons-U-turn-delights-United.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=5 February 2002 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Henry |last=Winter |title=Eriksson forced Ferguson into U-turn |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2308161/Eriksson-forced-Ferguson-into-U-turn.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=23 February 2007 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> Arsenal hit their stride as the 2001–02 season came to a close, winning the double for the second time in four years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal clinch Double |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1964495.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=8 May 2002 |access-date=1 January 2011 }}</ref> The championship was decided at Old Trafford in the penultimate game of the season; Wenger described his team's 1–0 win as a "shift of power."<ref>{{cite news |title=Wenger hails 'shift of power' |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/1976435.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=9 May 2002 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref>
{{Quote box |width=265px |bgcolor=#FFEFD5 |salign=left |align=right|quote="It's getting tickly now – squeaky-bum time, I call it." |source=—Sir [[Alex Ferguson]] on the title race, 2003<ref>{{cite news |title=Sir Alex Ferguson's best quotes |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/may/08/sir-alex-ferguson-best-quotes |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=8 May 2013 |access-date=22 August 2017}}</ref>}}
United again won the title back in [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2002–03]], when it looked as though Arsenal would retain it. A late-season encounter between the teams ended in controversial circumstances after the match officials allowed [[Thierry Henry]]'s second goal to stand despite the player being offside and [[Sol Campbell]] was sent off for an elbow on [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] in a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/2935603.stm|title=Highbury title deadlock|date=16 April 2003|access-date=8 November 2013|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Arsenal had beaten United on the way to [[2003 FA Cup final|FA Cup success]] and both teams contested the [[2003 FA Community Shield]] at the start of the [[2003–04 in English football|2003–04]] season. In a hotly-contested match, [[Phil Neville]] was booked in the first minute for a challenge on Vieira and a minute later, [[Ashley Cole]] received a booking for fouling Solskjær.<ref name="comc">{{cite news |title=Man Utd win Community Shield |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3125653.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=10 August 2003 |access-date=23 January 2011}}</ref> Yellow cards were also given to [[Quinton Fortune]] and [[Paul Scholes]] for United and Vieira for Arsenal.<ref name="comc"/> Substitute [[Francis Jeffers]] was shown a straight red for a kick on Phil Neville and, despite originally going unpunished, Campbell was later given a three-match ban by the FA for kicking out at [[Eric Djemba-Djemba]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Campbell charge deepens the rift |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/aug/20/newsstory.sport |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=20 August 2003 |access-date=23 January 2011 }}</ref> The game finished 1–1 after 90 minutes and United eventually won the Shield 4–3 on penalties.<ref name="comc"/>

===2003–04: Brawl and Cup semi-final meeting===
{{see also|Battle of Old Trafford}}
[[File:Old Traford.jpg|thumb|left|Old Trafford was the setting for another brawl between the two sides.]]
The rivalry escalated in September 2003, when Arsenal travelled to Old Trafford. In the match Vieira was shown a second yellow card for his part in an altercation with striker [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]], and during stoppage time, defender [[Martin Keown]] brought down [[Diego Forlán]] in the Arsenal penalty area. United were awarded a penalty and Van Nistelrooy stepped up to take it, but his shot rebounded off the crossbar.<ref name="deadl">{{cite news |last=McCarra |first=Kevin |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/sep/22/match.manchesterunited |title=Title rivals are reduced to spiteful stalemate |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=22 September 2003 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref>

This was followed by scenes of jubilation from the Arsenal players, who confronted Van Nistelrooy after his miss and the resulting scuffle led to another fracas after the final whistle.<ref name="deadl"/> The FA immediately took action, charging six of Arsenal's players ([[Jens Lehmann]], [[Ray Parlour]], [[Lauren (Cameroonian footballer)|Lauren]], Cole, Keown and Vieira) with improper conduct.<ref name="charg">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3128290.stm |title=Eight charged after bust-up |work=BBC Sport|date=24 September 2003 |access-date=2 July 2013}}</ref> The club was fined £175,000, the largest ever given to a club by the FA at the time.<ref name="charg"/> Lauren received a four-game ban, whereas Vieira and Parlour were given one-match suspensions.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/3228349.stm |title=Arsenal players banned |work=BBC Sport|date=30 October 2003 |access-date=23 August 2017}}</ref>

The next game between these two clubs was held at Highbury in March 2004, again ending in a draw following a late [[Louis Saha]] goal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3553027.stm |title=Arsenal 1–1 Man Utd |work=BBC Sport|date=28 March 2004 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> The match marked the first time a team had ever started the season reaching 30 games without defeat.<ref>{{cite news |last=Moore |first=Glenn |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/saha-takes-shine-from-arsenals-record-66504.html |title=Saha takes shine from Arsenal's record |date=29 March 2004 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=The Independent}}</ref>

Ferguson's side then knocked Arsenal out of the FA Cup semi-final at [[Villa Park]] the following weekend; United supporters at the ground led a chorus of "Where's your Treble gone?" to their rivals.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/apr/04/match.arsenal |title=United finally show mettle as Scholes delivers knockout blow |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |first=Amy |last=Lawrence |date=4 April 2004 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> United went on to win the FA Cup, while Arsenal regained the title without losing a league game.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/match_of_the_day/3913589.stm |title=Community Shield on MOTD |work=BBC Sport|date=21 July 2004 |access-date=23 August 2017}}</ref> They faced each other in the [[2004 FA Community Shield]] and Arsenal won the match 3–1.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2384307/Arsenal-show-there-is-life-beyond-Vieira.html |title=Arsenal show there is life beyond Vieira |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |first=Henry |last=Winter |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=23 August 2017}}</ref>
{{-}}

===2004–05: Unbeaten run ends, tunnel fracas, Cup final shootout===
{{see also|Battle of the Buffet}}
[[File:Arsène Wenger 2008.jpg|thumb|upright|Arsène Wenger was highly critical of [[Mike Riley (referee)|Mike Riley]]'s performance, suggesting the referee was biased towards the home side.<ref name="soup">{{cite news |first=Daniel |last=Taylor |title=Soup thrown at Ferguson in tunnel fracas |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/oct/25/newsstory.sport2 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=25 October 2004 |access-date=23 August 2017}}</ref>]]
By the time Arsenal next played Manchester United, the club had extended its unbeaten league run to 49 games.<ref>{{cite news |first=Russell |last=Thomas |title=Wenger draws on fountain of Arsenal youth |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/oct/18/match.sport8 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=18 October 2004 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> United stood in sixth place in the table, 11 points behind Arsenal and were intent on ending their rivals' undefeated streak.<ref name="fergm">{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Wilson |title=Fergie: Arsenal a 'mob who get away with murder' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/oct/17/newsstory.sport4 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=17 October 2004 |access-date=23 August 2017}}</ref> Ferguson in his press conference described Arsenal's conduct in the equivalent fixture a year ago as "...the worst thing I've seen in this sport. No wonder they were so delighted at the verdicts."<ref name="fergm"/>

The October 2004 league match, staged at Old Trafford, was blighted by a number of fouls, overlooked by referee [[Mike Riley (referee)|Mike Riley]], including striker Van Nistelrooy's studs-up challenge on Cole.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |title=Did Riley get the big calls right? |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3950865.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=25 October 2004 |access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref> Arsenal dictated much of the play, but as the game headed towards the finish, United threatened. The home side were awarded a penalty when [[Wayne Rooney]] was adjudged to have been fouled in the area by Campbell. Van Nistelrooy scored and late in the game Rooney scored to give United a 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Steve |last=Bartram |title=OT100 #83: Invincibles beaten |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/The-OT-100-News/2010/Feb/OT100-83-Invincibles-beaten.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140122122423/http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/The-OT-100-News/2010/Feb/OT100-83-Invincibles-beaten.aspx |publisher=Manchester United |date=2 February 2010 |archive-date=22 January 2014 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> Tempers flared in the tunnel afterwards; Wenger confronted Van Nistelrooy for his tackle on Cole, but Ferguson intervened and told him to leave his players alone.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wenger steps up row with Ferguson |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4178407.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=17 January 2005 |access-date=27 August 2015 }}</ref> Pizza was thrown at Ferguson by an Arsenal player, which forced him to change into the club tracksuit in order to carry out his television duties. An investigation into "Pizzagate" never came around as both clubs kept silent.<ref>{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Kay |title=FA aiming to shed light on what happened at end of the tunnel |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/article/fa-aiming-to-shed-light-on-what-happened-at-end-of-the-tunnel-xdtpwqxq56b |newspaper=The Times |date=26 October 2004 |access-date=27 August 2015 }} {{subscription required}}</ref>

The clubs met again five weeks later in the [[2004–05 Football League Cup|League Cup quarter-finals]] at Old Trafford and despite both sides fielding weakened teams, the match was not short of drama.<ref name="legcup">{{cite news |title=Man Utd 1–0 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/4047617.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=1 December 2004 |access-date=19 May 2012}}</ref> [[David Bellion]] gave United the lead in just 19 seconds, but tempers boiled over in the second half; a late tackle by [[Robin van Persie]] on [[Kieran Richardson]] resulted in a fracas between both sets of players, which concluded with both protagonists getting booked by referee [[Mark Halsey]].<ref name="legcup"/> The game finished 1–0.<ref name="legcup"/>

In the reverse league fixture, club captains Keane and Vieira had to be separated in the tunnel before the match by referee [[Graham Poll]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira fight in tunnel at Highbury |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vmv1l1oUHUA |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211115/Vmv1l1oUHUA |archive-date=15 November 2021 |url-status=live|website=YouTube | date=3 July 2007 |publisher=Irvine Ferris |access-date=15 February 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Keane accused the Arsenal midfielder of intimidating his teammate [[Gary Neville]], telling the press afterwards: "I said, 'Come and have a go at me'. Simple as that. If he wants to intimidate some of my team-mates then let's have a go at some of the other players. I think Gary Neville's an easy target. I wasn't having it."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/feb/02/newsstory.sport5 |title=Keane told Vieira: 'pick on me' |date=1 February 2005 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> Vieira gave Arsenal the lead in the eighth minute of the match but 10-man United ran out 4–2 winners.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal 2–4 Man Utd |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4221105.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=1 February 2005 |access-date=8 November 2013 }}</ref>

In May 2005, Arsenal and United contested the [[2005 FA Cup final|124th FA Cup final]]. It was the first time in the competition's history that the final was decided by a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Arsenal beat United 5–4, following a goalless draw after extra time.<ref name="fina">{{cite news |title=Arsenal 0–0 Man Utd (aet) |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/4558271.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=21 May 2005 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> Arsenal forward [[José Antonio Reyes]] became the second player in Cup final history to be sent off, following his second yellow card near the end of extra time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Amy|last=Lawrence |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/22/match.sport1 |title=Vieira holds his nerve to claim historic penalty prize for Arsenal |date=22 May 2005 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref>

===2005–2018===
[[File:Ferdinand Fabregas.jpg|thumb|left|upright|[[Rio Ferdinand]] and [[Cesc Fàbregas]] in discussion with the referee before the first European game between the two sides in April 2009.]]
[[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s emergence as title challengers put an end to Arsenal and Manchester United's domestic duopoly.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/wenger-fears-decade-chelsea-dominance-2397180 |title=Wenger fears decade of Chelsea dominance |date=20 May 2005 |website=Wales Online |location=Cardiff |access-date=28 August 2017 |quote=Chelsea now look to be the third force, if not the first one at the moment, and that will make it more interesting.}}</ref> The West London club won back-to-back league titles in [[2004–05 FA Premier League|2004–05]] and [[2005–06 FA Premier League|2005–06]] under [[José Mourinho]], at a time when Arsenal and United underwent a period of transition.<ref>{{cite news |first=Ian |last=Hughes |title=Rebuilt rivals set for battle |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7071519.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=2 November 2007 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Vieira and Keane had left their respective clubs by the end of 2005, while Ferguson came under intense scrutiny over his management.<ref>{{cite news |first=Richard |last=Williams |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/jan/02/sport.comment1 |title=Ferguson feeds critics a slice of humble pie, and it tastes good |date=2 January 2007 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Nevertheless, he guided his team to Premier League success in 2006–07, and won a further four league titles.<ref name="goldtit"/> At Arsenal, Wenger oversaw the club's relocation to the [[Emirates Stadium]] and made the decision to prioritise it over strengthening the squad.<ref name="reb">{{cite news |title=Young guns |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/aug/31/arsenal |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |first1=Alex |last1=Fynn |first2=Kevin |last2=Whitcher |date=31 August 2008 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> The club sold several experienced players, replenishing them with younger talent.<ref name="reb"/> The 2005 FA Cup win was their last piece of silverware until [[2014 FA Cup final|2014]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |title=Arsenal 3–2 Hull City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27354148 |work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2014 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref>

Though the rivalry cooled, the two clubs were still involved in engrossing battles; ''[[The Guardian]]'''s Jamie Jackson wrote after a November 2007 fixture: "For once here was enough spectacle to meet the pre-match hype and convince the millions watching around the world that the Premier League may just have the best footballers who can play the very best stuff."<ref>{{cite news |first=Jamie |last=Jackson |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/nov/04/match.arsenal |title=Last-gasp Gallas does level best for Gunners |date=4 November 2007 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> In 2009, the teams met in the semi-finals of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League]], which United won 4–1 on aggregate. United defender [[Patrice Evra]] was blunt in his post-match assessment: "It was 11 men against 11 children. We never doubted ourselves. We have much more experience and that's what made the difference."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/06/evra-manchester-united-arsenal-babies |title=United were a different class against Arsenal's 'children', says Evra |date=6 May 2009 |access-date=24 August 2017 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London}}</ref> Wenger described it as the most disappointing night of his career,<ref>{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/06/champions-league-arsenal-manchester-united-arsene-wenger-alex-ferguson |title=This was my worst night ever, admits Wenger, as Arsenal crash out |date=6 May 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> and said the response from Arsenal fans made him feel as though he had "killed someone".<ref>{{cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/16/arsene-wenger-arsenal-premier-league |title=Negative Arsenal fans make me feel like a murderer, says Arsène Wenger |date=16 May 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=The Guardian}}</ref>

[[File:Robin Van Persie MUFC 2013.jpg|thumb|[[Robin van Persie]] about to take a penalty against his former side, April 2013]]
Later that month, a 0–0 draw was enough to give United a third consecutive league title, equalling Liverpool's record of 18.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wilson |first=Paul |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/16/premier-league-manchester-united-arsenal1 |title=United retain Premier League crown after goalless finale at Old Trafford |date=16 May 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> Wenger paid his respects to Ferguson, saying that it was "remarkable to have such a consistent motivation at that level – and deal with the stress and all the other ingredients",<ref>{{cite news |last=Hayward |first=Paul |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/17/alex-ferguson-manchester-united-premier-league |title=Triumphant Sir Alex still defies the final whistle |date=17 May 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> and declared United worthy champions.<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8038259.stm |title=Man Utd 0-0 Arsenal |date=18 May 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In August of the following season, the two teams met at Old Trafford, with United coming from behind to win 2–1. Towards the end of the game, Arsenal had a goal ruled out for offside, causing Wenger to lash out and angrily kick a water bottle before being sent off by referee [[Mike Dean (referee)|Mike Dean]];<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8223417.stm |title=Man Utd 2-1 Arsenal |date=29 August 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> Wenger climbed on top of the dugout area, where he received chants of "sit down you paedophile" from United fans.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/man-utd-vs-arsenal/107237 |title=Diaby gaffe gifts United win |date=29 August 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=Sky Sports}}</ref> The incident resulted in an apology from referee's chief [[Keith Hackett]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8229352.stm |title=Wenger to get sending off apology |date=30 August 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> while United chief executive [[David Gill (football executive)|David Gill]] raised the issue with a group of influential supporters.<ref>{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/sep/03/arsene-wenger-chant-manchester-united |title=Manchester United asks fans to help end vile chants aimed at Arsène Wenger |date=3 September 2009 |access-date=29 August 2020 |work=The Guardian}}</ref>

In December 2010, Ferguson made a personal plea to the United fans to no longer sing the "sick" chant at Wenger, as those kind of chants from fans were considered an embarrassment to the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/dec/09/alex-ferguson-arsene-wenger-sick-chants|title=Sir Alex Ferguson calls for end to sick chants aimed at Arsène Wenger|last=Taylor|first=Daniel|date=9 December 2010|newspaper=The Guardian|access-date=9 December 2010|location=London}}</ref> With both teams going for the Premier League title in May 2011, Arsenal won their first game against Manchester United since November 2008, to leave United just three points ahead of Chelsea and six ahead of Arsenal going into the final three games of the season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/may/01/arsenal-manchester-united-premier-league |title=Arsenal beat Manchester United to breathe new life into title race |date=1 May 2011 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> Nevertheless, United won the league, nine points ahead of Chelsea and 12 points ahead of Arsenal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13444164 |title=Man Utd 4–2 Blackpool |date=1 May 2011 |work=BBC Sport|access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref>

In August 2011, Arsenal suffered their heaviest league defeat in 84 years as they lost [[Manchester United F.C. 8–2 Arsenal F.C.|8–2]] to Manchester United at Old Trafford. Arsenal had not lost a league game by such a margin since 1927 when they lost 7–0 to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the old [[Football League First Division]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arsenal.com/history/club-records/record-scorelines |title=Record Scorelines |publisher=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 July 2012}}</ref> This was also the first time they had conceded eight goals in a game since 1896, when they lost 8–0 to the now defunct [[Loughborough F.C.|Loughborough]] in the old [[Football League Second Division]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsene Wenger hurt by Arsenal 8–2 defeat at Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14703034 |work=BBC Sport|date=28 August 2011 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> A year later, striker Robin van Persie joined United, having stated that he would not renew his contract with Arsenal. It was speculated that he would move to a club overseas, but signed for the Manchester club, the first Arsenal player to do so since [[Viv Anderson]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20125835|title=Man Utd v Arsenal: Robin van Persie brave to move – Silvestre|last=Hafez|first=Shamoon|date=1 November 2012|work=BBC Sport|access-date=23 October 2014}}</ref> Ferguson called Wenger to push through a deal when he learnt of the contract situation.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Features/2012/Nov/sir-alex-ferguson-on-cantona-phone-call.aspx |title=Sir Alex: Van Persie signing evoked memories |last=Adam |first=Marshall |date=27 November 2012|publisher=Manchester United |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Van Persie was instrumental in United's league win of [[2012–13 Premier League|2012–13]] – Ferguson's last, and coincidentally received a [[Guard of honour#Association football|guard of honour]] by his former teammates before United faced Arsenal at the Emirates in April 2013.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal v Manchester United: Van Persie's guard of honour |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/22331826 |work=BBC Sport|date=28 April 2013 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref>

The appointment of Mourinho as United manager in 2016 added a new twist to the rivalry, given the previous animosity between him and Wenger.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Scott |last1=Patterson |first2=Tom |last2=Adams |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/english-premier-league/23/blog/post/2997960/united-vs-arsenal-rivalry-renewed-as-wenger-seeks-to-end-mourinho-curse |title=United vs. Arsenal rivalry renewed as Wenger seeks to end Mourinho curse |date=17 November 2016 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Sports writer [[Daniel Taylor (journalist)|Daniel Taylor]] however argued that Wenger's stagnation hindered any confrontations between the two managers, writing: "Ferguson stopped aiming his barbs at Wenger once it became clear his old enemy was no longer capable of producing title-winning teams and it doesn’t feel like a coincidence that Mourinho also seems indifferent now that Arsenal have dropped even further back."<ref>{{cite news |first=Daniel |last=Taylor |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/may/06/arsene-wenger-jose-mourinho-arsenal-manchester-united |title=Arsène Wenger's decline drains rivalry with José Mourinho of poison |date=7 May 2017 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> Former midfielder Phil Neville criticised the players for hugging in the tunnel before a league fixture in May 2017, calling the pleasantries a "total nonsense".<ref>{{cite news |title='Monreal thinks he's at a christening!' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/39840515 |work=BBC Sport|date=7 May 2017 |access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> In December 2017 analysts calculated the league fixture between the two sides as the Premier League's first billion pound game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal v Man Utd set to be Premier League's first 'billion-pound game' |url=http://www.eurosport.com/football/premier-league/2017-2018/arsenal-v-man-utd-set-to-be-premier-league-s-first-billion-pound-game_sto6428261/story.shtml |publisher=Eurosport |date=1 December 2017 |access-date=2 December 2017}}</ref> 

The swap deal of Arsenal’s [[Alexis Sánchez]] and United’s [[Henrikh Mkhitaryan]] during January 2018 brought about fellness to the rivalry and is one of the most infamous transfer deals in English football history. Ahead of Wenger's last game against United in April 2018, [[Channel 5 (British TV channel)|Channel 5]] aired an hour-long documentary titled "The Feud", described in a review by ''[[The Guardian]]'' as "exhilarating".<ref>{{cite news |last=Smyth |first=Rob |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/apr/19/alex-ferguson-arsene-wenger-manchester-united-arsenal-tv-documentary-feud |title=When Arsène Wenger and Alex Ferguson fought bitterly to be top dog |date=19 April 2018 |access-date=27 August 2020 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> In the build-up to the game, Ferguson paid tribute to Wenger, saying he had always respected him in spite of the rivalry, and that the two clubs had "made the Premier League".<ref>{{cite news |last=Dollard |first=Rory |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/premier-league/i-always-did-really-respect-the-man-alex-ferguson-leads-tributes-to-arsene-wenger-at-old-trafford-36856114.html |title='I always did really respect the man' – Alex Ferguson leads tributes to Arsene Wenger at Old Trafford |date=29 April 2018 |access-date=27 August 2020 |work=[[Irish Independent]]}}</ref> United fans gave Wenger a standing ovation prior to the game at Old Trafford, which ended in a 2–1 defeat through a last-minute goal from [[Marouane Fellaini]], a result described as "cruel yet predictable"; Arsenal had won one game in 15 years as the away team in the fixture.<ref>{{cite news |last=Critchley |first=Mark |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/arsene-wenger-leaves-arsenal-next-manager-manchester-united-match-report-things-we-learned-a8328511.html |title=Arsene Wenger's last visit to Old Trafford ended in fitting style – with a cruel yet predictable defeat |date=29 April 2018 |access-date=27 August 2020 |work=[[Irish Independent]]}}</ref>
{{-}}

==Ferguson and Wenger==
It was not until Wenger's arrival in October 1996 that Arsenal reemerged as a serious league competitor. By the end of the 1996–1997 season, Manchester United amassed their fourth title in five seasons,<ref>{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Holt |title=Rivals bestow new title upon United |newspaper=The Times |page=48 |date=7 May 1997}}</ref> whereas Arsenal finished the campaign in third – their highest position since the formation of the Premier League in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Full Arsenal league record, from 1893/94 to 2005/06 |url=http://www.arseweb.com/history/league_pos.html |website=Arseweb.com |access-date=20 August 2017 |archive-date=21 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170821004511/http://www.arseweb.com/history/league_pos.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> During the season, Wenger commented on rule changes which permitted an extension to the league calendar: "It's wrong the programme is extended so Manchester United can rest and win everything."{{sfn|Manson|2005|p=89}} His observation irked Ferguson, who replied: "He has no experience of English football. He has come here from Japan, and now he is telling everyone how to organise our football. Unless you have been in the situation and had the experience then he should keep his mouth shut, firmly shut."<ref>{{cite news |title=Wenger, in the words of others |url=https://www.fifa.com/live-scores/nationalleagues/nationalleague=england-premier-league-2000000000/news/newsid/230/062/2/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826110457/http://www.fifa.com/live-scores/nationalleagues/nationalleague=england-premier-league-2000000000/news/newsid/230/062/2/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 August 2016 |website=FIFA.com |date=21 March 2014 |access-date=15 August 2016}}</ref>

The relationship between both managers was evidently hostile to begin with. Ferguson noted that Wenger was the only manager he came across in the league not to share a drink with after matches – an English football "tradition".<ref>{{cite news |title=French lessons: How Wenger changed English football |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/oct/01/sport.comment1 |first=Amy |last=Lawrence |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=1 October 2006 |access-date=25 March 2014}}</ref> In 2009, Wenger said his discourtesy was mistaken for mistrust and managers "cannot be completely friendly and open up."<ref name="wengint">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/arsene-wenger-interview-the-full-transcript-of-matthew-syeds-interview-ws2f3pn0cbb|title=Arsene Wenger interview: The full transcript of Matthew Syed's interview}}</ref> When asked if this was the reason he avoided the post-match drink, he replied: "Most of the time, yes. What can you say if you have won? And if you have lost all you want to do is get home and prepare for the next game."<ref name="wengint"/>

[[File:Alex Ferguson.jpg|thumb|upright|Sir Alex Ferguson's relationship with Arsène Wenger turned cordial in later years.]]
In January 2005, Ferguson and Wenger were embroiled in a new row over what had happened in the tunnel after ''Pizzagate''.<ref name="embro">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4183811.stm |title=The Wenger and Ferguson diaries |work=BBC Sport|date=23 January 2005 |access-date=15 August 2016}}</ref> Ferguson alleged that Wenger called his players "cheats" and never apologised for his team's behaviour: "It's a disgrace, but I don't expect Wenger to ever apologise, he's that type of person."<ref name="embro"/> Wenger then claimed Ferguson was guilty of bringing the game into disrepute; he told reporters that he "will never answer any questions any more about this man," but went further to question the motive of the press: "What I don't understand is that he does what he wants and you are all at his feet."<ref>{{cite news |title=Ferguson's explosive attack lights Wenger's touch-paper |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/fergusons-explosive-attack-lights-wengers-touch-paper-487056.html |first=James |last=Lawton |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=17 January 2005 |access-date=15 August 2016}}</ref> Both managers came under pressure from the [[Metropolitan Police Service]], then Sports Minister [[Richard Caborn]] and Premier League chairman [[Richard Scudamore]] to put an end to the bickering.<ref>{{cite news |title=The bickering years |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2354648/The-bickering-years.html |first=John |last=Ley |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=1 February 2005 |access-date=25 March 2014}}</ref> Ferguson and Wenger agreed to tone down their words, in an attempt to defuse the rivalry. In later years, Ferguson said Arsenal's defeat "scrambled Arsène’s brain" and caused their relationship to breakdown for almost five years.<ref name="autobf">{{cite news |title=Arsène Wenger rift revealed in Alex Ferguson book |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/Sir_Alex_Ferguson/10396056/Arsene-Wenger-rift-revealed-in-Alex-Ferguson-book.html |first=Jeremy |last=Wilson |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=22 October 2013 |access-date=25 March 2014}}</ref>

The two managers have "exchanged some of football's best and bitterest verbal swipes," according to ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/6104349/Sir-Alex-Ferguson-and-Arsene-Wenger-their-bitter-football-rivalry-in-words.html |title=Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger: their bitter football rivalry in words |date=28 August 2009 |access-date=25 March 2014 |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London}}</ref> In 1997, Ferguson called Wenger a "novice" for complaining about the fixture programme and later said of his linguistic skills: "They say he’s an intelligent man, right? Speaks five languages! I've got a 15-year-old boy from the Ivory Coast who speaks five languages!"<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/5254011/the-war-of-words |title=The war of words |publisher=Sky Sports |date=5 May 2009 |access-date=15 August 2016}}</ref> After Arsenal's defeat to Manchester United in February 1997 – a match marred by a bust up between Wright and Schmeichel, Wenger referred to Ferguson's interference: "I was surprised to see Ferguson on the pitch because you can only play eleven."{{sfn|Manson|2005|p=89}} When Ferguson asserted that his team played the best football in England during the 2001–02 season, Wenger quipped: "Everyone thinks they have the prettiest wife at home," a remark that Ferguson initially suspected was a taunt at his own wife Cathy.{{sfn|Crick|2003|p=585}}

Such was the media's fascination of both managers' insults towards one another, psychologists were brought in to read and contrast their personalities.{{sfn|Manson|2005|p=89}} John Kramer, a sports psychologist suggested in 2004 that Ferguson and Wenger used their rivalry in order to relax before an important match. To him, Ferguson was "...the past master in terms of creating an environment of keeping his players hungry" by using a persecution complex; Wenger on the other hand diffuses the psychology and would rather "...tell his players they are all superb and will attempt to create an environment where they are able to show off their skills without the rest of it."<ref name="physc">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3758916.stm |title=All in the mind |first=Jonathan |last=Stevenson |work=BBC Sport|date=20 October 2004|access-date=25 March 2014}}</ref> Kramer concluded that both managers' comments "add[s] to the drama", but was insignificant in the games between the two clubs.<ref name="physc"/>

Ferguson in his autobiography said a major turning point in his relationship with Wenger was after the Champions League semi-final of 2009; the Arsenal manager invited his competitor into the dressing room and congratulated him on United's win.<ref name="autobf"/> Wenger said their relationship had become genial since his team stopped competing with Manchester United for trophies.<ref name="wengint"/> The move to the Emirates Stadium in 2006 is often cited as the reason why, given it coincided with a transitional phase for the club. Several experienced first teamers were displaced in favour of youth and the style of football became shifted more towards ball retention.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2009/may/28/barcelona-champions-league-arsene-wenger |newspaper=The Guardian|first=Richard |last=Williams |location=London |date=28 May 2009 |access-date=28 June 2013 |title=Barcelona's triumph holds hope for Arsène Wenger's brand of football}}</ref> Ferguson assessed the change in philosophy proved that Wenger did not "like to blend them too much with older players;" he also felt the team lacked a much needed balance between attack and defence.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/arsenal/4785524/Arsenal-lack-balance-in-transfer-dealings-says-Manchester-Uniteds-Alex-Ferguson.html |title=Arsenal lack balance in transfer dealings, says Manchester United's Alex Ferguson |first=Emily |last=Benammar |date=23 February 2009 |access-date=25 March 2014 |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London}}</ref>

==Television and radio broadcasts==
The growth of the rivalry during the 1990s attracted the attention of broadcasters and has led to fixtures being rescheduled from the [[English football on television#3pm .22Blackout.22|3 pm blackout period]] to primetime viewing in the United Kingdom. League matches are often broadcast on [[Sky Sports]] – once as early as 11:15 am,<ref>{{cite news |first=Richard |last=Alan |title=TV's Football Dinners |page=B11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=8 March 1998}}</ref> while cup games have aired on mainstream channels, [[BBC One]] and [[ITV (TV channel)|ITV]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The FA Cup, 2014–15, Man United v Arsenal |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b055mszt |publisher=BBC|access-date=17 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= Magic of the Cup? Manchester United complete decade of televised FA Cup ties |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/jan/17/manchester-united-cambridge-fa-cup |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=17 January 2015 |access-date=17 August 2016}}</ref> At the height of the rivalry, the games on Sky had been billed as title deciders, and play was summarised by [[Martin Tyler]] and [[Andy Gray (footballer, born 1955)|Andy Gray]].{{sfn|Gray|2005|p=254}} The April 2003 match at Highbury, advertised as "Face Off",<ref>{{cite news |first=Dan |last=Rookwood |title=Richard Keys |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/may/09/newsstory.sport |website=The Guardian|date=9 May 2003 |access-date=17 August 2016}}</ref> was seen by a British audience of 3.4&nbsp;million,<ref>{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Wells |title=Niche TV overtakes big five in ratings battle |page=7 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=25 April 2003}}</ref> while the 2005 FA Cup final was watched by more than 480&nbsp;million viewers worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |title=A history of the FA Cup |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/More/History |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=17 August 2016}}</ref>

In August 1999, the two sides participated in the world's first [[Sky Sports Active|interactive]] football match,<ref>{{cite web |title=Sky: 20 years on&nbsp;... |url=http://corporate.sky.com/documents/pdf/publications/sky_20 |publisher=BSkyB|year=2009 |access-date=17 August 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930001233/https://corporate.sky.com/documents/pdf/publications/sky_20 |archive-date=30 September 2015}}</ref> and 11 years later featured in the world's first 3D TV sports broadcast – both events trialled by Sky.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/7121293/Arsenal-v-Manchester-United-broadcast-live-in-3D-on-Sky-Sports.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |title=Arsenal v Manchester United broadcast live in 3D on Sky Sports |date=31 January 2010 |access-date=17 August 2016 }}</ref> To commemorate the 80th anniversary of the first radio football commentary, the BBC reintroduced its "grid system" to help listeners visualise the action between Arsenal and Manchester United in January 2007.<ref name="radio">{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Fletcher |title=Singer Gray in commentary box |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/6266771.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=18 January 2007 |access-date=17 August 2016}}</ref> Musician [[David Gray (British musician)|David Gray]] was enlisted as guest summariser, with [[John Murray (sports broadcaster)|John Murray]] describing the action and [[James Alexander Gordon]] calling out the grid numbers to explain where the ball was.<ref name="radio"/>

The rivalry was explored in an [[ITV4]] special, ''Keane & Vieira: Best of Enemies'', first broadcast in December 2013. The documentary saw the former captains discussing about their relationship, views on their respective managers and what they thought of each other.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.itv.com/presscentre/ep1week50/keane-and-vieira-best-enemies |publisher=ITV Press Office |title=Keane and Viera Best of Enemies ITV4 |date=9 December 2013 |access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref>

===Hat-tricks===
Eleven players have scored a [[Hat-trick#Association football|hat-trick]] in a competitive match between Arsenal and Manchester United.

===Records===
*First competitive meeting: '''Newton Heath 3–3 Woolwich Arsenal''' – Second Division, 13 October 1894<ref name="stats"/>
*First FA Cup meeting: '''Manchester United 2–3 Arsenal''' – Fourth round, 10 March 1906<ref name="stats"/>
*First Community Shield meeting: '''Arsenal [[1948 FA Charity Shield|4–3]] Manchester United''' – 6 October 1948<ref name="stats"/>
*First League Cup meeting: '''Arsenal 3–2 Manchester United''' – Second round, 30 August 1977<ref name="stats"/>
*First European meeting: '''Manchester United 1–0 Arsenal''' – UEFA Champions League semi-final, 6 April 2009<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/apr/30/patrice-evra-manchester-united-arsenal |title='We could have won 4–0,' says disappointed Patrice Evra |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=30 April 2009 |access-date=21 August 2017}}</ref>
*First away victory:
**Arsenal: '''Manchester United 0–1 Arsenal''' – Second Division, 15 March 1902<ref name="stats"/>
**Manchester United: '''Arsenal 0–2 Manchester United''' – Second Division, 3 April 1897<ref name="stats"/>
*Highest scoring game: '''[[Manchester United F.C. 8–2 Arsenal F.C.|Manchester United 8–2 Arsenal]]''' – Premier League, 28 August 2011<ref name="stats"/>
*Largest winning margin:
**Arsenal: '''5–0''' – FA Cup fourth round, 30 January 1937<ref name="stats"/>
**Manchester United: '''8–2''' – Premier League, 28 August 2011<ref name="MUNARS"/>
*Most consecutive wins:
**Arsenal: '''4''' (9 November 1997 – 20 September 1998, 22 January 2023 – 4 December 2024)<ref name="MUNARS"/>
**Manchester United: '''5''' (6 September 1983 – 24 August 1985)<ref name="stats"/>
*Longest undefeated run:
**Arsenal: '''7''' (22 January 2023 – 17 August 2025; 5 wins and 2 draws)<ref name="MUNARS"/>
**Manchester United: '''9''' (20 November 1954 – 11 October 1958; 6 wins and 3 draws; 19 October 1991 – 22 March 1995; 3 wins and 6 draws)<ref name="mufcinfo"/>
*Most consecutive draws: '''4''' – 16 April 2003 to 28 March 2004<ref name="stats"/>
*Most meetings in a season: '''5''' – [[1998–99 in English football|1998–99]] and [[2004–05 in English football|2004–05]]<ref name="stats"/>
*Most goals: '''12''' – Wayne Rooney (Manchester United)<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/incoming/who-liverpool-fcs-goalscoring-nemesis-11622846 |title=Who is Liverpool FC's goalscoring nemesis? |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |date=15 July 2016 |access-date=28 August 2017 |quote=Rooney has scored 14 goals in total against Arsenal, his first two as an Everton player.}}</ref>
*Most appearances: '''50''' – Ryan Giggs (Manchester United)
*Highest league attendance: '''83,260''' at [[Maine Road]], First Division, 17 January 1948<ref>{{cite news|last=Slater|first=Chris|title=Grounds for celebration? Anniversary of City and United's historic stadium-share deal|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/grounds-celebration-anniversary-city-uniteds-7216102|work=Manchester Evening News|date=4 June 2014|access-date=24 November 2020}}</ref>
